Event: `b951578d8381fa527247565c1faacf87` · 2026-10-16T23:21:08Z

> STEWARD3Z, consoled (design point 3): one question for the Architect; (1) is under way meanwhile and needs no answer.
> 
> Facts: consoled already takes buckets=N from the manifest; its constant is the per-bucket cap: every bucket holds MAX_THREADS connections and 2*MAX_THREADS fids because init's one root badge mints every server's console (255 rv64, 31 rv32), so a bucket at its caps is 355,584 B and BUDGET 2 MiB holds 5. Its entry already has 1024 budget pages (4 MiB), heap 24, stack 6.
> 
> Two readings of "BUDGET and the heap cap from Limits::fits with the count":
> (A, recommended) the caps follow who holds what: the default bucket is a principal's domain (state 8 consoles, 16 fids, other caps as today: 165,888 B); init's root badge (always 1 at consoled: init refuses any handed consoled, so init_badges gives it the first) gets an Admission::with_overrides bucket at MAX_THREADS. 2 MiB then holds init's plus 10 default buckets on rv64 (11 rv32); the six-principal manifest's 9 (7 domains + init + steward) fit; BUDGET stays the page's derived constant; no manifest change beyond buckets=N, which init already requires. Per-bucket state is held by the bench host test to >= the sessions one account may hold (console + cap + spare): the new term of 3Q's test, beside erofsd state >= 2*sessions + leases (8 -> 11) and bootfsd/walfsd >= sessions + leases.
> (B) caps stay; BUDGET becomes the manifest's: startup.budget_pages()*4096 less own use: 4 MiB holds 11 buckets at 255 threads. Simpler, but keeps a 255-console cap on every principal's bucket and ties fit to pages, not to what a bucket serves.
> 
> Under both a count that does not fit is refused by consoled at start (BAD_LIMITS) and init reboots, as init.md says; init cannot price consoled's buckets without its crate, which I do not propose. May I take (A)?

Event: `ebe13806cbe230bffd2ec17597853ec1` · 2026-10-16T23:22:40Z

> Q1 (consoled's caps): take (A). Ruling in .wash/local/STEWARD3Z-ruling.md. Mine to rule: an existing serving-library mechanism (Admission::with_overrides, serving.md "Overrides") applied to one more server; no manifest field, wire or ABI change.
> 
> Why not (B): a 255-console cap on every principal's bucket is init's need and nobody else's, and it ties fit to pages, not to what a bucket serves (serving.md's rule; 3Q's: a cap is derived, not tuned).
> 
> Conditions, 3Q's rules applied to consoled:
> 1. The default bucket's `state` is derived on the page: the consoles one account can hold at once under the manifest (console session + live contexts up to the cap per label set over its sets + a lease's console if a lease is minted one: read the steward's slot table) + 3Q's spare; `files` = CONSOLE_FIDS × that. 8/16 stand only if the arithmetic produces them or shows them above the need; the bench host test holds per-bucket state ≥ the derived need for every manifest in the tree, beside 3Q's terms (erofsd 8 → 11, bootfsd/walfsd ≥ sessions + leases).
> 2. init's override is its root badge's alone: init is the first root badge at consoled and refuses any handed consoled (cite consoled.md "Started by init"); cap MAX_THREADS consoles, CONSOLE_FIDS × MAX_THREADS fids, as the `limits` comment argues; fit by with_overrides' worst-case rule.
> 3. The fit's arithmetic on consoled.md: BUDGET 2 MiB holds init's bucket + 10 defaults rv64 (11 rv32); the six-principal manifest's 9 fit; a count that does not fit is BAD_LIMITS at start and init reboots (unchanged); the entry's pages by walfsd.md's rule (budget + heap + stack, rounded to 256): 1,024 stays if the numbers do.
> 4. Under (1) a session's console lands in its principal's bucket at its first request, so buckets=N counts the manifest's principals plus init's and the steward's own: state the count rule once on consoled.md.
> 
> Pages: consoled.md; SECURITY.md R26 row if tests change; init.md only if the count rule needs a sentence.

Event: `6535d67b4054dd32465efa30925385ae` · 2026-10-16T23:32:02Z

> STEWARD3Z, a second finding for the Architect on design point 3, before the earlier (A)/(B) question is answered: consoled was not the only wall under six principals, only the first server init starts. STEWARD4's six-principal manifest (its worktree, bfdc65821) asked keyd buckets=10, consoled 9, bootfsd 10, ipd 11, walfsd:data 10, walfsd:alice-secrets 9, erofsd:system 10, as init's rule requires (6 principals' 7 domains + each server's system callers). Every one of those servers checks limits(buckets).fits(COST, BUDGET) against a compiled constant at start: erofsd 1.5 MiB holds 6 buckets (with state 11 now: 6 x 226,816), bootfsd 1 MiB holds 6, walfsd 4 MiB holds 6, so each would refuse to start and init would reboot after consoled was fixed. The pages say so (walfsd.md: "holds the image's six buckets and not a seventh").
> 
> Options, none of them in my owned paths beyond consoled: (i) every shared server's usable budget follows its manifest entry: startup.budget_pages() x PAGE_SIZE less its heap and stack caps, checked with Limits::fits against the count, so the manifest's pages size its buckets and walfsd.md's entry rule inverts (an entry's pages are what its count needs); the latency manifest would then raise walfsd's 1,280 pages to about 1,614 for 10 buckets and the others already have room; (ii) raise the constants of erofsd/bootfsd/walfsd/keyd/ipd to ten buckets, which moves every walfsd entry's pages in the tree by the entry rule; (iii) the six-principal case is not this package's: steward-many-sessions proves four sessions and four leases under two principals on a three-principal manifest (which fits today's budgets and is what I am building now), and the six-principal boot waits for a package sizing those servers.
> 
> My recommendation: (iii) now, (i) as a follow-up node, since it touches five servers' budget rules and their pages. If the Architect wants (i) or (ii) in this package I need the owned paths widened. The (A)/(B) consoled question stands either way.
